text:
alex: kicked off a hetero-kernel sanity bench across us-central / eu-west to repro the p95 spikes we've been seeing when kernel fallthroughs happen. testing Llama-13B / Mistral-7B / Qwen-7B with long context (4k-16k).

jia: nice. did you pin sequences? what batch sizes?

alex: seqs=4096 and 16384, batch 1/4/8. auto kernel selection on. command I used:

alex: ```
bench-run --model qwen-7b --seq 16384 --batch 4 --gpu h100 --region eu-west1 --kernel auto --warmup 200 --samples 100
```

bench-bot: Scheduled bench job job-4421 on h100-eu-west1, ETA ~12m. Logs will be here: https://ci.redwood.local/job-4421

sasha: saw a few fallthrough logs in the H100 run earlier:

sasha: ```
[WARN] kernel_selector: fallthrough to fallback_kernel 'naive_attn' for model=qwen-7b seq=16384 reason=missing_optimized_kernel
[INFO] runtime: switching to fallback kernels increased mem-bandwidth usage by ~12%
```

marco: what were the P50/P95 numbers per GPU? rough is fine.

alex: ok rough consolidations across models (seq=16k, batch=4):
- H100 (eu): Llama-13B p50=220ms p95=1.8s, Mistral-7B p50=180ms p95=1.2s, Qwen-7B p50=250ms p95=2.4s
- A100 (us): Llama-13B p50=260ms p95=2.1s, Mistral-7B p50=210ms p95=1.5s, Qwen-7B p50=300ms p95=3.0s
- MI300 (us): Llama-13B p50=200ms p95=1.6s, Mistral-7B p50=170ms p95=1.1s, Qwen-7B p50=230ms p95=2.0s

alex: note the p95 blowups align with the kernel fallthrough log entries. small spike windows ~500-800ms extra when fallback kicks in mid-request.

jia: that matches earlier suspicion — hetero kernel availability across regions is inconsistent so routing + fallback causes tail latency. Did you capture which kernels were missing?

alex: yes, for Qwen-7B the optimized rope_gqa kernel (rope_gqa_longseq_v2) was missing on older H100 images in eu-west1. A100 images had a different compiled binary that used generic gqa_v1 instead of v2. MI300 had v2 everywhere.

sasha: so we have mismatch: some fleets compiled with kernel v2, others fell back to naive_attn or generic_gqa. That explains per-region delta.

marco: capacity sizing implication? if we plan for p95 SLO 1s for seq=16k, what headroom to reserve if fallthroughs unpredictable?

yuki: quick back-of-envelope: assume baseline p95 without fallthrough ~1.2s for qwen on h100, fallback adds median +0.7s spike. To be safe keep 25-30% extra reserved and prefer routing policy to avoid nodes lacking v2.

alex: another quick mitigation: ensure kernel catalog sync during image build and add a canary job that verifies presence of rope_gqa_longseq_v2 for onboarding models.

alex: sample canary script I used:
```
# verify kernels
redwood-kernel-check --image gcr.io/redwood/h100:2026-03-15 --expect rope_gqa_longseq_v2,qkv_fuse_v3
```

sasha: +1 on adding canary and failing deploys if critical kernels missing. we should also add a metric: kernel_fallback_rate per node.

marco: for immediate prod, recommend: (1) mark nodes without v2 as lower priority for longseq traffic, (2) lift weight to mi300 pools for longseq customers, (3) roll image with kernel sync.

jia: I'll open a quick PR to routing to prefer nodes with kernel tag `has_rope_gqa_v2` for routes that request seq>=8k.

yuki: also worth adding a regression alert in Optimize: when p95 increases >20% + fallback_rate >0.5% then page oncall.

alex: agreed. i'll aggregate full CSV of runs and post link when done. bench-bot: job-4421 completed and CSV uploaded: https://ci.redwood.local/job-4421/results.csv

bench-bot: NOTE: job-4421 had 7 fallback events across 100 samples (fallback_rate 7%).

sasha: thanks — that fallback_rate explains the noisy tails. next steps: routing PR + canary + metrics. I'll own the metrics dashboard.

marco: I'll coordinate a patch roll for eu-west H100 images to add v2 kernels. ETA tomorrow morning.

alex: awesome. thanks all. I'll post the CSV and a short summary in the eng-ml channel after I clean numbers. :thumbsup:
